In [[general topology]], a '''saturated set''' is a subset of a [[topological space]] equal to an [[intersection (set theory)|intersection]] of (an arbitrary number of) [[open set]]s.

== Definition ==
Let <math>S</math> be a subset of a [[topological space]] <math>X</math>. The '''saturation''' <math>\operatorname{sat}(S)</math> of <math>S</math> is the intersection of all the [[neighborhood (topology)|neighborhood]]s of <math>S</math>.<ref name="Martin"/>{{rp|380, Definition 2.22}}
:<math>\operatorname{sat}(S)=\bigcap\mathcal N_S</math>
Here <math>\mathcal N_S</math> denotes the [[neighborhood filter]] of <math>S</math>. The neighborhood filter <math>\mathcal N_S</math> can be replaced by any [[local basis]] of <math>S</math>. In particular, <math>\operatorname{sat}(S)</math> is the intersection of all open sets containing <math>S</math>.

Let <math>S</math> be a subset of a [[topological space]] <math>X</math>. Then the following conditions are equivalent.
* <math>S</math> is the intersection of a set of open sets of <math>X</math>.
* <math>S</math> equals its own saturation.
We say that <math>S</math> is '''saturated''' if it satisfies the above equivalent conditions.<ref name="Martin"/>{{rp|380, Definition 2.22}}<ref name="FFS">{{cite journal |last1=Finocchiaro |first1=Carmelo A. |last2=Fontana |first2=Marco |last3=Spirito |first3=Dario |title=The upper Vietoris topology on the space of inverse-closed subsets of a spectral space and applications |language=en |journal=Rocky Mountain Journal of Mathematics |volume=48 |issue=5 |pages=1551–1583 |date=2018 |issn=0035-7596 |doi=10.1216/RMJ-2018-48-5-1551 |mr=3866559 |zbl=1444.54001 |arxiv=1805.12454}}</ref>{{rp|1556}} We say that <math>S</math> is '''recurrent''' if it intersects every non-empty saturated set of <math>X</math>.<ref name="Martin"/>{{rp|395, Definition 5.1}}

== Properties ==
=== Implications ===
Every [[Gδ set|G<sub>δ</sub> set]] is saturated, obvious by definition. Every recurrent set is [[dense set|dense]], also obvious by definition.

=== In relation to compactness ===
A subset of a [[topological space]] is [[compact set|compact]] if and only if its saturation is compact.

For a topological space <math>X</math>, the following are equivalent.
* Every point <math>x\in X</math> has a compact [[local basis]]. (This is one of several definitions of [[locally compact space]]s.)
* Every point <math>x\in X</math> has a compact saturated local basis.

In a [[sober space]], the intersection of a [[downward-directed set]] of compact saturated sets is again compact and saturated.<ref name="Martin"/>{{rp|381, Theorem 2.28}} This is a sober variant of the [[Cantor intersection theorem]].

=== In relation to Baire spaces ===
For a [[topological space]] <math>X</math>, the following are equivalent.
* <math>X</math> is a [[Baire space]].
* Every recurrent set of <math>X</math> is Baire.
* <math>X</math> has a Baire recurrent set.

== Examples ==
For a [[topological space]] <math>X</math>, the following are equivalent.
* Every subset of <math>X</math> is saturated.
* The only recurrent set of <math>X</math> is <math>X</math> itself.
* <math>X</math> is a [[T1 space|T<sub>1</sub> space]].

A subset <math>S</math> of a [[preordered set]] <math>(X,\lesssim)</math> is saturated with respect to the [[Scott topology]] if and only if it is [[upward-closed set|upward-closed]].<ref name="Martin">{{cite journal|access-date=2022-07-09 |archive-date=2021-05-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210510085554/http://topology.nipissingu.ca/tp/reprints/v24/tp24219.pdf |date=1999 |first1=Keye |format=PDF |issn=0146-4124 |issue=Summer |journal=Topology Proceedings |language=en |last1=Martin |mr=1876383 |pages=375–405 |title=Nonclassical techniques for models of computation |url=http://topology.nipissingu.ca/tp/reprints/v24/tp24219.pdf |url-status=live |volume=24 |zbl=1029.06501}}</ref>{{rp|380}}

Let <math>(X,\lesssim)</math> be a [[closed preordered set]] (one in which every [[chain (order theory)|chain]] has an [[upper bound]]). Let <math>\max X</math> be the set of [[maximal element]]s of <math>X</math>. By the [[Zorn lemma]], <math>\max X</math> is a recurrent set of <math>X</math> with the [[Scott topology]].<ref name="Martin"/>{{rp|397, Proposition 5.6}}
